blocks.body: # AI Sales Recommendation System — Cybersecurity & AI Risk Assessment

## Executive Summary

**The immediate decision is to complete discovery and governance before accepting production risk.** The synthetic reference assessment identifies credible customer-data disclosure, recommendation manipulation, ML supply-chain compromise, privileged misuse, availability, privacy, fairness and drift scenarios. Five of ten inherent risks are provisionally critical.

**The repository is decision support—not an authorization to operate or a compliance certificate.** Company architecture, data, controls, legal duties, owners, appetite and residual-risk decisions remain unverified.

## Decision requested

Name the business, system, data, model, security, privacy/legal and residual-risk owners; approve the discovery and five EBIOS workshops; and authorize read-only collection of production evidence. Keep any deployment advisory-only, with human review and override, until the decision boundary and measurable acceptance criteria are approved.

## Risk picture

**The highest-priority paths combine ordinary enterprise compromise with AI lifecycle leverage.** Compromised identities can expose customer data; poisoned inputs or unauthorized model promotion can alter recommendations at scale; a compromised dependency can reach build credentials, training, model artifacts and serving.

## Evidence completed

The laboratory includes a reproducible synthetic dataset and model, authenticated and validated FastAPI inference, model-artifact digest verification, advisory-only human review, drift and group-performance procedures, OWASP Threat Dragon modeling, NIST OSCAL validation, pytest, Ruff, Bandit, pip-audit, Trivy and Syft evidence.

**Automated checks prove bounded procedures, not production control effectiveness.** The final images contain three critical and thirteen high Debian advisories per image, all currently unfixed; Trivy found no image secrets or configuration findings. Runtime pip and setuptools were removed to reduce attack surface.

## Recommended next steps

1. **Confirm scope and accountability:** business purpose, users, decisions, prohibited uses, data, third parties, owners and risk appetite.
2. **Run all five EBIOS workshops:** replace assumptions, validate sources/scenarios, agree severity/plausibility and assign treatments.
3. **Assess production controls:** identity, least privilege, encryption, logging, lineage, approval/promotion, rollback, resilience and incident response.
4. **Define AI acceptance criteria:** validity, calibration, segment performance, drift, latency, availability, explanation, override, contest and redress.
5. **Close supply-chain gaps:** immutable trusted sources, lock/hashes, vulnerability and license triage, isolated builds, signed provenance and policy enforcement.
6. **Authorize or reject explicitly:** an accountable human records residual risk, conditions and expiry only after evidence and retest.

## Further questions

- Which real decision is influenced, and can a recommendation disadvantage a person or customer?
- Is the interface internal-only, and which identities can read data, train, approve, deploy or audit?
- Which customer fields, labels and sensitive/proxy attributes are used, retained or logged?
- Who supplies code, models, data and infrastructure, and what provenance is verified?
- What accuracy, calibration, group-performance, drift, availability and abuse thresholds stop the system?
- Who may override, contest, investigate, roll back and accept residual risk?

## Caveats and assumptions

- All business and production-system facts are assumptions until stakeholder validation.
- Risk scores are ordinal workshop inputs, not measured probabilities or financial loss estimates.
- Synthetic model metrics do not establish business fitness, fairness, safety or legal compliance.
- A SHA-256 manifest detects alteration only if the manifest and verification root are trusted.
- Scanners can miss vulnerabilities and can surface non-runtime components; raw evidence and triage rationale are both retained.
- Selected NIST controls require organizational tailoring, implementation statements, assessment and authorization.

## Method and authoritative references

The assessment connects the [ANSSI EBIOS Risk Manager method](https://messervices.cyber.gouv.fr/guides/en-ebios-risk-manager-method) to the [NIST Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf), [NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final), and the [NIST AI RMF](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework). Threat research is mapped to [MITRE ATLAS](https://atlas.mitre.org/) and the [OWASP Machine Learning Security Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-machine-learning-security-top-10/).
